about: ix's layers, checked by tests/test_layering.py on every test run with the shared checker (components/capabilities/_testing/layers.py), which reads a map as slick crafting-aces' layer-check.py does, so the same file runs under that script too. Adopted from the reviewed map (scratch/review-2026-10-22/ix-layers.json, at 1580c81) and fitted to ix as it now is: provenance in the domain and its adapter, the compose environment, matrix_calls. The inner layers' allowances copy test_layering.py's allowlists, so the two checks agree. 'why' keys are read by neither checker.
scan_why: Every Python file in the package, so a new module that no layer claims fails the suite. Tests are out of scan: a test reaches adapters by design.

why.stdlib: pure computation only (test_layering's PURE_STDLIB): no clock, random source, filesystem or network
why.pydantic, pydantic_core: every record is a pydantic model, and PydanticCustomError is how a validator names the shape it refused
why.ix.domain: domain/__init__ re-exports the ports, and the plan states what a port needs
why.files by name: domain/ports.py is a layer of its own, so the domain's files are named; a new domain module is added here on purpose
why.forbid: matrix runs an experiment and is named only by the root and the matrix_* adapters; OpenTelemetry is one adapter's; the builtin open is I/O no import shows

why.ix.domain: a port is stated in the domain's types: Subject, Probe, Sensor, Environment, Scope and the optional Traced, Review, StandIn, Preflight and Liveness speak in experiments, runs and problems
why.nothing else: ix keeps its ports inside the domain package, so this layer is a file, not a folder

why.asyncio: carrying a trial out waits, times out and races a stop flag (test_layering's LAYER_STDLIB); the domain has none
why.ix.domain, ix.application: the use cases run over the ports, in the domain's types

why.nothing: packages that hold the genre and kind YAML for the ix.genre and ix.kind entry points; importing one runs its __init__ (SECURITY.md), so it runs nothing

why.*: one technology each: k6, ps, httpx, child Python, docker compose, git and file digests, the registration file, pydantic-evals
why.ix.domain: the ports they implement and the types they speak in
why.ix.adapters._out: one adapter may build on another, a subject or the compose environment on the launcher's processes module; a deviation from the four places that test_layering allows on purpose
why.forbid: matrix and OpenTelemetry each have adapter files of their own

why.*: matrix is their technology: agent runtimes and sessions (matrix_agents, matrix_calls, matrix_judge), the loader (matrix_documents), errors (matrix_errors), process groups (matrix_process), the run store and executor (matrix_runs)
why.ix.adapters._out: matrix_judge builds on matrix_agents and matrix_calls; matrix_runs brings the compose environment down with the run

why.opentelemetry: the one file that speaks the OpenTelemetry API; it implements the Traced and Span shapes structurally, so it needs nothing of ix

why.matrix: matrix drives ix's run path through these components, and hands them its Inputs and RunContext
why.ix.domain, ix.application: a driving adapter calls the use cases, in the domain's types

why.ix: the command reaches ix through 'import ix' alone. The entry admits every ix.* path, since an allowance is a prefix; test_layering holds the command to ix.__all__

why.ix.composition, ix.domain: the library surface names the root and the domain, never an adapter or a use case: which adapters are bound is not its decision
why.importlib, os: the version from the installed distribution; the run directory's environment default

why.*, ix: the root chooses adapters through matrix's registry, wires ports and holds settings: the one layer that reaches everything

single_importer_why: one file per technology: the OpenTelemetry API (the command installs a provider through matrix), the readiness probe's HTTP client, the command line, pydantic-evals' evaluators and the pydantic-ai model a dry-run judge evaluator stands in on (both imported inside the adapter's functions, so ix starts without them). docker and the launcher cannot be held here: docker is a program named in a string, and the launcher's technology is reached as 'from matrix import process', which an import check reads as 'matrix'. test_layering holds both
